display_title: Speed up symbolic shape polynomial arithmetic and comparisons.

head_commit.message:
Speed up symbolic shape polynomial arithmetic and comparisons.

Comparing and combining symbolic dimension expressions allocates per-call closures during syntactic ordering, checks normalization on scopes with no normalization rules, and runs full polynomial `divmod` (constructing both quotient and remainder expressions on failure) even when leading terms are not divisible.

Inline `_syntactic_cmp` across `_DimFactor`, `_DimTerm`, and `_DimExpr` without closure allocations (removing the unused `cmp_comparable` and `cmp_sequence` helpers), short-circuit unit-term multiplication and empty scope normalization rules, and add a `_DivModOp` fast path in `__floordiv__` and `__mod__` when the leading term is not divisible. Also update `shape_poly_benchmark` for internal `core.canonicalize_slice` and `_DimExpr._leading_term` renames.

display_title: Handle near-singular covariances in jax.random.multivariate_normal.

head_commit.message:
Handle near-singular covariances in jax.random.multivariate_normal.

`jax.random.multivariate_normal` defaults to `method='cholesky'`, which returns `NaN` when floating-point rounding makes small eigenvalues of a singular or ill-conditioned covariance matrix non-positive. `method='eigh'` could also return `NaN` on singular or near-singular matrices when rounding produced tiny negative eigenvalues before `sqrt`.

Clamp negative eigenvalues to zero in `method='eigh'`, and update the `multivariate_normal` docstring with usage examples and guidance on sampling directly from a factor `F` when `cov = F @ F.T` is already factored, adding diagonal jitter, or using `method='eigh'` / `method='svd'`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/14345

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Adjust strides/sizes/shapes for sub-byte memrefs fully in `ctx.async_copy`.

We introduce a new transform `SubBytePackingTransform` which does that fully on the Python side, making the code in `runtime.cc` unnecessary.

This also fixes a particular bug: in the test example `dyn_base_indices` were (0, 256) previously, where minor most dim is the number of bytes.
But the expected value is to have 128 bytes for 4-bit data type. Here we make sure we make the minor-most contiguous dim packed.
Essentially we copied `[0:64, 512:768]`, instead of `[0:64, 256:512]`.

[Mosaic GPU][NFC] Simplify MMA descriptor and instruction helpers.

`mma_utils` and `tcgen05` accumulated redundant branching and indirection around byte-stride conversion, small-tile contiguity checks, instruction descriptor construction, and inline PTX lowering.

Unify element-to-byte stride conversion and express small-tile contiguity checks directly in terms of `swizzle_elems` in `mma_utils.create_descriptor`. Fold `create_scaled_f8f6f4_instr_descriptor` and `create_scaled_f4_instr_descriptor` into `_create_scaled_instr_descriptor`, merge the sparse and dense `create_instr_descriptor` dispatch in `tcgen05`, and drop unused PTX register declarations.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [Pallas:MGPU] Use logical shapes for TMEM refs in run_scoped.

head_commit.message:
[Pallas:MGPU] Use logical shapes for TMEM refs in run_scoped.

Previously, `GPUMemoryRef.get_ref_aval()` still wrapped 3D+ TMEM refs in a `TransformedRef` over a collapsed 2D physical `AbstractTMEMRef`, requiring `run_scoped`, `pallas_call`, and GPU interpret mode to unpack `TransformedRef` scratch arguments via `wrap_with_transforms`, `aval_transforms`, and `kernel_arg_transforms`.

Return a plain `AbstractTMEMRef` with its logical shape from `GPUMemoryRef.get_ref_aval()` so `ScratchShape.get_ref_aval()` always returns an `AbstractRef`. Track TMEM `CollapseLeadingBatchDimensionsTransform` entries through `ref_transforms` and `ModuleContext.scratch_transforms` (both standalone and inside `RefUnion`) so `ModuleContext.alloc_tmem` and `_extract_aliased_ref` allocate the collapsed 2D physical TMEM layout while `_handle_transforms` prepends the inverse expansion during lowering. With all `get_ref_aval()` implementations returning `AbstractRef`, remove `wrap_with_transforms`, `kernel_arg_transforms`, and `apply_layout_transforms` from `run_scoped`, `pallas_call`, and GPU interpret mode.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Add jax.lax.asinpi, acospi, atanpi, and atan2pi.

head_commit.message:
Add jax.lax.asinpi, acospi, atanpi, and atan2pi.

Computing inverse trigonometric functions in half-revolutions by dividing `jnp.asin`, `jnp.acos`, `jnp.atan`, or `jnp.atan2` by `pi` rounds an irrational number after computing the angle. That extra rounding step introduces small errors and misses exact rational values at special inputs, such as `acospi(-1) = 1` or `atanpi(1) = 0.25`.

Add `jax.lax.asinpi`, `jax.lax.acospi`, `jax.lax.atanpi`, and `jax.lax.atan2pi` (and their core primitives) to compute `asin(x) / pi`, `acos(x) / pi`, `atan(x) / pi`, and `atan2(x, y) / pi` directly. Each returns exact results at special inputs (`0`, `±1`, `±inf`, and axis-aligned inputs) and avoids overflow or underflow when computing `atan2pi(x, y)` on very large or very small numbers.

Also register `sinpi`, `cospi`, and `tanpi` alongside the new primitives in Pallas cost estimation, move the `sinpi`, `cospi`, and `tanpi` special-value tests out of `lax_test.py` into per-op special-value tests in `tests/numerics/trig_test.py`, and share the inverse-trig test point lists as module constants.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Write persistent compilation cache entries atomically

head_commit.message:
Write persistent compilation cache entries atomically

`LRUCache.put` wrote entries in place with `write_bytes`, so another process
sharing the cache directory could read a partially written entry, and a
process killed mid-write left a truncated entry behind. Since `put` returned
early when the entry already existed, a truncated entry was never replaced:
every later process failed to read it and recompiled.

On local filesystems, `put` now writes the entry to a uniquely named
temporary file in the cache directory, fsyncs it and renames it into place
with `os.replace`, replacing any existing entry. The temporary file is
removed if the write fails. This restores what the old `GFileCache` did.
Remote filesystems keep the previous behaviour, since rename is not atomic
there in general.

Fixes #42197.

head_commit.message:
Add `low`, `high`, and `highest` sampling precision modes to `jax.random.normal`

Adds an optional `mode` parameter (`"low"`, `"high"`, `"highest"`, defaulting to `"low"`) to `jax.random.normal`, with default controlled by the `jax_random_normal_mode` config option:

- `mode="low"` keeps the existing behavior of mapping a float with random mantissa bits through `erf_inv`, which cuts off around `+/-5.3` standard deviations for `float32`.

display_title: Make jnp.interp match numpy.interp when fp contains infinite values

head_commit.message:
Make jnp.interp match numpy.interp when fp contains infinite values

jnp.interp evaluated fp[i-1] + t * (fp[i] - fp[i-1]), which is NaN at and
around any knot whose value is +inf or -inf (inf - inf, 0 * inf). numpy
returns the knot value at an exact knot, re-evaluates from the other end
of the interval when the first form is NaN, and returns the shared value
when both ends of the interval are equal, so interpolating a table of
log-probabilities that contains -inf gives -inf, not NaN.

Apply the same three rules, but only where the original expression is
already NaN and x is not NaN. Finite inputs, `left`/`right`, `period`
and the gradients with respect to x and fp are unchanged, and a NaN in x
or in fp still propagates.

head_commit.message:
Include static_argnums, static_argnames and keep_unused in the jit C++ cache key

The C++ dispatch cache is shared between all jit instances of the same
Python function whose JitGlobalCppCacheKeys compare equal. The per-call
signature records the values of the static arguments and the avals of the
dynamic ones, but not which positions are static, so two jit instances of
one function with different static_argnums (or static_argnames) hit the
same entry whenever the dynamic avals and the static values coincide, and
the executable compiled for the first instance runs with the arguments of
the second:

  def g(a, b): return a * 10 + b
  x = jnp.float32(2.)
  jax.jit(g, static_argnums=0)(1, x)   # 12.0
  jax.jit(g, static_argnums=1)(x, 1)   # 12.0, should be 21.0

jnp.interp hits this through the public API because it builds a jit
instance of _interp per call, with left/right/period static only when they
are None or a string: jnp.interp(x, xp, fp, right=1) after
jnp.interp(x, xp, fp, left=0) with the same shapes returns the result of
the first executable with 1 fed into its `left` input.

Add static_argnums, static_argnames and keep_unused (which changes the
compiled executable's parameter list) to JitGlobalCppCacheKeys. The key is
only hashed when a jit instance is created, so cached dispatch is
unaffected. The new fields do not take part in contains_explicit_attributes,

display_title: Fix tail sampling accuracy in jax.random.truncated_normal.

head_commit.message:
Fix tail sampling accuracy in jax.random.truncated_normal.

Fixes #10951.

Previously, `jax.random.truncated_normal` computed inverse-CDF samples by drawing `u ~ uniform(key, shape, dtype, minval=erf(lower / sqrt(2)), maxval=erf(upper / sqrt(2)))` and evaluating `sqrt(2) * erf_inv(u)`. This suffered from several floating-point accuracy issues in the tails:
- `uniform` generated a fixed-point grid of resolution `2^(-nmant)` in `[0, 1)` and rescaled via `floats * (b - a) + a`, cutting off upper-tail probabilities below `2^(-nmant)` on wide intervals, clamping `floats == 0` draws to the lower bound, and losing mantissa bits when adding `a` near ±1 (causing a fraction of draws to round to ±1 and clamp to the far boundary).
- At extreme truncation bounds where `erf` saturates to ±1 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/10951), `a == b == ±1` caused `erf_inv(u)` to return `±inf` and clamp all samples to the wrong boundary.
- For 16-bit dtypes (`bfloat16`, `float16`), native 7-bit/10-bit uniform grids and early `erf` saturation degraded tail accuracy even on moderate bounds.

Update `_truncated_normal` to:
- Promote `<32`-bit dtypes (`bfloat16`, `float16`) to `float32` for quantile interpolation and inverse-CDF evaluation before casting back to `dtype`.
- Reflect intervals with positive midpoint (`flip = lo > -hi`, `(a, b) = (-hi, -lo)`) so tail bounds always lie in `(-inf, 0]`, where `ndtr(x) -> 0` retains full floating-point exponent precision down to `finfo.tiny`.
- Draw open-interval uniforms `u` in `[2^-(nmant + 1), 1.0)`, interpolate `p = clip(pa + u * (pb - pa), finfo.tiny, 1.0 - min_u)` in `ndtr` space, invert via `erf_inv_core(..., has_far_tail=True, is_ndtri=True)`, and negate when `flip` is true.

head_commit.message:
[Pallas] Validate shard containment and resolve static local offsets in `shard_map` fusion

When pushing outer prologue or epilogue operations across `jax.shard_map`, `_extract_local_block` previously sliced each pulled block out of the device's local shard without checking per-shard containment:
- When a pulled block dimension had the same size `b` as the local shard dimension `size` (`b == size`), `_extract_local_block` took an unconditional `start = 0` shortcut without verifying `block_start == shard_start` (silently reading wrong shards on `jnp.reshape(..., out_sharding=P("y", "x"))` or size-1 slices of length-1 shards).
- When `b != size` on a sharded axis, `s_idx` was traced so `_extract_local_block` fell through to `lax.dynamic_slice(x, [start - s_idx * size], sizes)`, which silently wrapped negative local offsets (`lax._dynamic_slice_indices`) or clamped out-of-shard offsets, and failed Mosaic TPU lowering even when `start - s_idx * size` was a constant per-shard offset.

This change hardens and deduplicates `shard_map` fusion:
- Unify containment checking and local-shard slicing into `_make_block_extractor` in `shard_map_fusion.py`, using `jax._src.export.shape_poly` (`symbolic_shape` + `symbolic_dim_bounds`) over manual mesh axis coordinates without enumerating mesh points to verify `0 <= local_start <= local_start + b <= shard_size` (raising `NotImplementedError` on cross-shard operations or outer scalar prefetch) and emit static `lax.slice` (or identity) whenever local offsets are constant across shards.
- Reuse `pallas_core._canonicalize_block_shape`, `pallas_core._get_block_shape`, `pallas_core._get_start_index` (shared with `GridMapping.compute_start_indices_interpret`), `pallas_core.default_index_map`, `block_spec._is_squeezed`, `shard_map._manual_spec`, and `jax.NamedSharding.shard_shape`, and drop the `numpy` dependency from `shard_map_fusion.py`.
- Deduplicate scalar-prefetch jaxpr extraction across `_pull_block_transform` and `_push_block_spec` into `_make_scalar_prefetch_fn` (evaluated via `make_kernel_function`), share `pvary_operands` across `block_spec.py` and `shard_map_fusion.py`, and unify fusible discovery across `jaxpr_fusion.py` and `shard_map_fusion.py` via `_fusible_eqns`.

head_commit.message:
Use jax.lax.atanpi and atan2pi in internal callers.

Update internal JAX callers that divide inverse trigonometric results by `pi` (or convert them directly to degrees) to use `jax.lax.atanpi` and `jax.lax.atan2pi`:

- `jax.scipy.stats.cauchy.cdf` and `logcdf` (and `sf`/`logsf`, which call them): evaluate with a single `lax.atan2pi` call (`atan2pi(scale, loc - x)` for `cdf`, and `log(p)` / `log1p(-p)` with `p = atan2pi(scale, |x - loc|)` for `logcdf`) to avoid tail cancellation and `(x - loc) / scale` overflow.

- `jax.numpy.angle(..., deg=True)`: compute `180 * lax.atan2pi(im, re)` directly so axis and diagonal angles are exact in degrees.
- `jax.scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation`: compute `as_euler` in half-turns with `lax.atan2pi` and wrap via `angles - 2 * round(0.5 * angles)`, use `lax.sinpi`/`lax.cospi` in `from_euler(..., degrees=True)`, and pass `degrees` as a static `excluded` argument to the `vectorize` helpers.

head_commit.message:
[Pallas] Cache lowered `pjit` helper functions in Mosaic TPU lowering.

`jaxpr_subcomp` previously cached individual primitive lowering rules via `_emit_pallas_lowering_rule_as_fun`, while `pjit` equations inside a Pallas kernel body were inlined into the caller block on every call (`pjit` was in `_uncacheable_primitives`). When a `@jax.jit`-decorated helper function is invoked repeatedly inside a kernel body with identical input/output abstract values and parameters, inlining duplicates its entire MLIR body at every call site.

Allow `pjit.jit_p` equations whose body `Jaxpr` is closed and free of uncacheable primitives (`_is_cacheable_jaxpr`) to be lowered once into a cached `func.FuncOp` and called at each call site. display_title: Implement scipy.special.ndtri_exp in JAX as jax.scipy.special.ndtri_exp.

head_commit.message:
Implement scipy.special.ndtri_exp in JAX as jax.scipy.special.ndtri_exp.

Evaluating `ndtri(exp(y))` directly returns `-inf` once `exp(y)` underflows to zero in the left tail, loses precision near the median `y = -log(2)` where `2 * exp(y) - 1` cancels, and loses precision near `y = 0` where `exp(y)` rounds toward 1.

`ndtri_exp(y)` splits `(-inf, 0]` into three regions sharing a single `exp`, `expm1`, `log`, and `sqrt` evaluation:
1. Near the median `y = -log(2)`: shifts `y + log(2)` without rounding error and evaluates a polynomial approximation around zero.
2. Moderate tails (down to `log(2 * tiny)`): rewrites the inputs to `erf_inv_core`'s polynomial tables using `exp` and `expm1` so `y` stays in log space instead of round-tripping through `exp` and `log` or subtracting nearly equal numbers.
3. Far left tail (down to `-fmax`): inverts the asymptotic expansion of `log_ndtr` with one Newton step using `(hi, lo)` pairs of floats for extra precision.

Custom JVP rules express the tail derivatives in terms of `erfcx` so `exp(x^2 / 2)` cancels analytically instead of overflowing, and compute higher-order derivatives via a closed two-variable polynomial system in `g = x'(y)` and `h = 1 + x * g`. Worst-case primal error is 0.5 ULP (`bfloat16`), 1.0 ULP (`float16`), 3.0–3.5 ULP (`float32`), and ≤ 2.5 ULP (`float64`).

display_title: Use jax.lax.atanpi and atan2pi in internal callers.

head_commit.message:
Use jax.lax.atanpi and atan2pi in internal callers.

Update internal JAX callers that divide inverse trigonometric results by `pi` (or convert them directly to degrees) to use `jax.lax.atanpi` and `jax.lax.atan2pi`:

- `jax.scipy.stats.cauchy.cdf` and `logcdf` (and `sf`/`logsf`, which call them): evaluate with a single `lax.atan2pi` call (`atan2pi(scale, loc - x)` for `cdf`, and `log(p)` / `log1p(-p)` with `p = atan2pi(scale, |x - loc|)` for `logcdf`) to avoid tail cancellation and `(x - loc) / scale` overflow.
- `jax.scipy.special.owens_t`: use `0.5 * lax.atanpi(modified_a)` for the `h = 0` special case.
- `jax.numpy.angle(..., deg=True)`: compute `180 * lax.atan2pi(im, re)` directly so axis and diagonal angles are exact in degrees.
- `jax.scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation`: compute `as_euler` in half-turns with `lax.atan2pi` and wrap via `angles - 2 * round(0.5 * angles)`, use `lax.sinpi`/`lax.cospi` in `from_euler(..., degrees=True)`, and pass `degrees` as a static `excluded` argument to the `vectorize` helpers.

display_title: Add jax.lax.asinpi, acospi, atanpi, and atan2pi.

head_commit.message:
Add jax.lax.asinpi, acospi, atanpi, and atan2pi.

Computing inverse trigonometric functions in half-revolutions by dividing `jnp.asin`, `jnp.acos`, `jnp.atan`, or `jnp.atan2` by `pi` rounds an irrational number after computing the angle. That extra rounding step introduces small errors and misses exact rational values at special inputs, such as `acospi(-1) = 1` or `atanpi(1) = 0.25`.

Add `jax.lax.asinpi`, `jax.lax.acospi`, `jax.lax.atanpi`, and `jax.lax.atan2pi` (and their core primitives) to compute `asin(x) / pi`, `acos(x) / pi`, `atan(x) / pi`, and `atan2(x, y) / pi` directly. Each returns exact results at special inputs (`0`, `±1`, `±inf`, and axis-aligned inputs) and avoids overflow or underflow when computing `atan2pi(x, y)` on very large or very small numbers.

Also register `sinpi`, `cospi`, and `tanpi` alongside the new primitives in Pallas cost estimation, move the `sinpi`, `cospi`, and `tanpi` special-value tests out of `lax_test.py` into per-op special-value tests in `tests/numerics/trig_test.py`, and share the inverse-trig test point lists as module constants.
